Option A fits because the current code already has one settings path for this view. Defaults live in `settings/resolver.ts:12`, and their resolved values flow to `ui/report-view.ts:30`. The new setting would use that same path and that same consumer. A view-local settings object would create a second source of truth for this view's settings. Defaults would then come from two places, and later changes would have to keep them in sync. Reusing the resolver adds no new boundary.

The setting needs a defined behavior. You described filters that stay active after a workspace switch and hide rows. What should the new setting control, and what should its default be?

A) It controls whether report filters reset on a workspace switch. The default is reset, so the hidden-rows problem goes away unless a user opts to keep filters.
B) It controls whether report filters reset on a workspace switch. The default is keep, so today's behavior stays the same until a user opts in.
C) Other - name it.

Recommendation: A - The reported problem is rows hidden in the new workspace, and resetting by default fixes that. Users who want filters to carry over can still keep them.

What should the new setting make filters do when switching workspaces?
A) Reset by default, with an option to preserve filters.
B) Preserve by default, with an option to reset filters.
C) other - name it.
Recommendation: A - it addresses rows unexpectedly being hidden in the new workspace while retaining an opt-in for the current behavior.
